note: Wildflower orchard site in Wongan Hills listed by the tourism board

name: Kulin
note: Wheatbelt town known for its tin horse roadside art and Bush Races, with a museum and the Jilakin Rock nearby

name: Corrigin
note: Wheatbelt town known as a Town of Windmills, with a dog cemetery, pioneer museum and the Dog in a Ute statue

name: Southern Cross
note: Goldfields-edge Wheatbelt town on the Great Eastern Highway, a Golden Pipeline stop with a history museum

name: Wiluna
note: Outback town at the start of the Canning Stock Route, with a Martu art gallery and a discovery centre

name: Sandstone
note: Murchison gold town with wide heritage streets, a heritage trail and London Bridge nearby

name: Tin Horse Highway
note: Roadside art trail of over 100 tin horses lining the road out of Kulin, a quirky open-air gallery

name: West Kulin Tin Horses
note: Group of tin horses on the western side of Kulin, an introduction to the Tin Horse Highway

name: Kulin Museum
note: Local museum in Butler's Garage, one of Kulin's original buildings, with a large collection of local history

name: Buckley's Breakaway
note: Breakaway landform near Kulin with a contrast of colours, a picnic and photography stop

name: Kulin Giant Waterslide and Aquatic Centre
note: Regional Wheatbelt aquatic centre with a large waterslide, open in summer

name: Corrigin Dog Cemetery
note: Pet cemetery established 1974 with over 200 dogs buried, 5 km west of Corrigin

name: Corrigin Pioneer Museum
note: Local museum with old restored farm machinery telling Corrigin's pioneer history

name: Corrigin Rock
note: Large rocky outcrop just east of Corrigin with views over the town

name: Dog in a Ute Statue
note: Statue in Corrigin commemorating the 2002 world-record convoy of 1527 utes with dogs

name: London Bridge
note: Natural basalt bridge 3 km south of Sandstone, about 350 million years old, a stop on the Sandstone Heritage Trail

name: Sandstone Heritage Trail
note: Self-drive and town walk of 18 km past Sandstone's historic buildings and natural sites

name: Sandstone Heritage Museum and Visitor Centre
note: Small heritage museum with gold rush and pastoral artefacts, where trail brochures are sold

name: Tjukurba Art Gallery
note: Working gallery of Martu artworks and historic photos in Wiluna, a must-see on the town's cultural side

name: Canning-Gunbarrel Discovery Centre
note: Museum in the restored old Wiluna hospital telling the story of the Canning Stock Route and the town

name: Canning Stock Route
note: 1800 km desert stock route from Wiluna north to Halls Creek, a four-wheel-drive journey starting in Wiluna

name: Wiluna Red Hill Lookout
note: Rocky rise 1.2 km south of Wiluna with views across the town to the gold mine

name: Wiluna Clay Pans
note: Clay pans just out of Wiluna that fill after rain, for picnics and bird watching

name: Wiluna North Pool
note: Peaceful waterhole 15 km from Wiluna among red earth and gum trees, for a picnic or sunset

name: Last of the Nomads Statue
note: Statue in Wiluna honouring Warri and Yatungka, believed to be the last of the Mandildjara people

name: Wiluna Pioneer Cemetery
note: Pioneer cemetery in Wiluna with graves dated from 1893 to 1903

name: Wiluna Heritage Walk
note: Self-guided heritage walk through Wiluna with a brochure from the shire office or post office

name: Yilgarn History Museum
note: Museum in Southern Cross with artefacts, records and memorabilia of the Yilgarn district

name: Pathways to Wave Rock
note: 760 km self-drive trail through Wheatbelt towns to Wave Rock

name: Dalgaranga Meteorite Crater
note: Meteorite crater: 24 m across and 3 m deep, Australia's smallest impact crater, on Dalgaranga station; daylight access, signposted, no facilities. Sits about 75 km west of Mount Magnet and 100 km north of Yalgoo, so it may fall in the Murchison (golden-outback) region; the proposer should resolve. [Moved from wa-coral-coast at reconciliation: the Murchison inland is wa-golden-outback (wa-regions.md).]

name: Yalgoo
note: Town: Mid West wildflower-route town (Shire of Yalgoo) and the gateway to the Dalgaranga crater; Wikipedia places it in the Mid West, though the region list does not name it, so the proposer should confirm the boundary. [Moved from wa-coral-coast at reconciliation: the Murchison inland is wa-golden-outback (wa-regions.md).]
